summary.text: Shelley Moore Capito is the incumbent Republican U.S. Senator from West Virginia, seeking a third term in 2026. A former college counselor and state delegate, she served in the U.S. House from 2001 to 2015 before her election to the Senate in 2014. She chairs the Senate Committee on Environment and Public Works.

paragraphs.text: Shelley Moore Capito was born Shelley Moore on November 26, 1953, in Glen Dale, West Virginia, the daughter of former Gov. Arch A. Moore Jr.

Capito earned a bachelor's degree from Duke University and a master's degree in education from the University of Virginia, then worked as a college counselor and as director of an educational information center.
She represented Kanawha County in the West Virginia House of Delegates from 1997 to 2001.

Capito was elected to the U.S. House in 2000 and served seven terms representing West Virginia's 2nd Congressional District, from 2001 to 2015; she was the first Republican woman elected to Congress from West Virginia. She founded the Congressional Coal Caucus after an explosion that killed 29 coal workers and is a former chairwoman of the Congressional Caucus for Women's Issues.
She was elected to the Senate in 2014, becoming the first woman elected to the Senate from West Virginia, and was re-elected in 2020, defeating Democrat Paula Jean Swearengin.

In the 2025-2026 session Capito chairs the Environment and Public Works Committee and sits on the Commerce, Science, and Transportation; Appropriations; and Rules and Administration committees. She chairs the Appropriations subcommittee on Labor, Health and Human Services, Education, and Related Agencies.
She is married to Charles Capito, and they have three children, according to Wikipedia.
